item.title: 1985: Brewers Release Rollie Fingers, 39, After 17 Seasons
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers unconditionally release future Hall of Famer Rollie Fingers, 39, ending a 17-season career that produced 944 games pitched (all but 37 in relief), 114 victories, 341 saves, three World Series rings, one MVP Award, one Cy Young Award, and seven All-Star selections. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 2023: Guardians Add Espino to 40-Man Roster to Protect Him
item.description: The Guardians selected Espino's contract on November 14, 2023, adding him to their 40-man roster in order to protect him from the Rule 5 draft. Photo: Erik Drost (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2022: Williams Named Rays' New Third Base Coach
item.description: On November 14, 2022, Williams was officially announced as the Rays' new third base coach, replacing Rodney Linares. Photo: Joel Dinda (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2018: González Traded to Pirates for Moroff and Luplow
item.description: On November 14, 2018, González (along with minor leaguers Tahnaj Thomas and Dante Mendoza) were traded to the Pittsburgh Pirates in exchange for Max Moroff and Jordan Luplow. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2015: Red Sox Acquire Four-Time All-Star Closer Craig Kimbrel
item.description: The Boston Red Sox announced the acquisition of four-time, All-Star closer Craig Kimbrel from the San Diego Padres in return for prospects Manuel Margot, Javier Guerra, Carlos Asuaje and Logan Allen. In dealing Margot and Guerra, the Red Sox took advantage of two of the deeper positions in their minor league system. Photo: Dirk Hansen (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2014: Rays Trade Hellickson to Diamondbacks for Two Players
item.description: On November 14, 2014, the Rays traded Hellickson to the Arizona Diamondbacks for Andrew Velazquez and Justin Williams. Photo: Derral Chen on Flickr (Original version) 佾珜 (Crop) (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2013: MLB Unanimously Approves Funding for Expanded Instant Replay
item.description: Major League Baseball takes the first vote in a two-step process, unanimously approving funding for expanded instant replay in the 2014 MLB season. They plan to approve the new rules when they meet on January 16 in Paradise Valley, Arizona, after agreements with the unions for umpires and players. The instant replay was first used by the NFL in 1986, the NHL in 1991, the NBA in 2002 and Wimbledon in 2006.

item.title: 2013: Snyder Signs Minor League Deal With Texas Rangers
item.description: On November 14, 2013, Snyder signed a minor league contract with the Texas Rangers. Photo: Minda Haas on Flickr (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2005: Alex Rodriguez Beats out Ortiz to Win Second MVP
item.description: Alex Rodriguez of the New York Yankees beats out David Ortiz of the Boston Red Sox to win his 2nd career MVP Award, becoming the first Yankee to win the honor since Don Mattingly in 1985. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1988: Angels Hire Doug Rader, 44, as 1989 Manager
item.description: The California Angels fill their 1989 managerial vacancy by hiring former 5x NL Gold Glove-winning third baseman and one-time Texas Rangers skipper Doug Rader, 44. Owner Gene Autry admits he initially offered the post to Gene Mauch, who has already served two terms in the job and resigned twice, in 1982 and again this past March, when he stepped down in the middle of spring training for health reasons. Photo: Jerry Reuss (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1983: Bruce Bochte, 33, Signs With Athletics After Year Off
item.description: First baseman/outfielder Bruce Bochte, who sat out the 1983 season in retirement, signs with the Oakland Athletics as a free agent. Bochte, 33, batted .290 with 697 hits in 681 games for the 1978–1982 Seattle Mariners and was an AL All-Star in 1979.

item.title: 1981: Indians Trade Duane Kuiper, 31, to Giants for Whitson
item.description: The Cleveland Indians trade second baseman Duane Kuiper to the San Francisco Giants for pitcher Ed Whitson. Kuiper, 31, is destined to become a popular, longtime member of the Giants' broadcasting team after his playing days end in 1985. Photo: Bruce Washburn Arbor to SJ (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1979: Dodgers Sign Pitcher Dave Goltz, Free Agent From Twins
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers sign pitcher Dave Goltz, granted free agency from the Minnesota Twins on November 1. Photo: Los Angeles Dodgers (Public domain).

item.title: 1971: Luis Tiant Throws 3-0 No-Hitter in Venezuelan Winter League
item.description: In Venezuelan Winter League, Luis Tiant of the Tiburones de la Guaira hurls a 3–0 no-hitter against his former team Leones del Caracas. Tiant becomes the fourth pitcher in the league's 26-year history to achieve the feat, joining Len Yochim (1955), Mel Nelson (1963) and Howie Reed (1968). Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1968: Willie Sherdel, 72, Pitcher for Cardinals and Braves
item.description: "Wee Willie" Sherdel, 72, left-handed pitcher who won 165 games (losing 146) for the St. Louis Cardinals (1918–1930 and 1932) and Boston Braves (1931–1932); member of 1926 world champions.

item.title: 1966: George Weiss Retires as Mets President, Bing Devine Succeeds
item.description: George Weiss retires as president of the New York Mets and is succeeded by his top aide, Bing Devine. Weiss will be elected to the Hall of Fame in 1971 for his prior accomplishments as an executive with the New York Yankees, while Devine makes significant contributions to the 1969 "Miracle Mets" during his brief term as president/GM.

item.title: 1961: Charles Hurth, 55, Resigns as Mets General Manager
item.description: Charles Hurth resigns as general manager of the New York Mets, a post he's held since April 1960 when the team—then without a name—was a member of the proposed Continental League. Hurth, 55, a former longtime minor-league executive related by marriage to the Branch Rickey family, had remained general manager after the franchise was formally admitted as an expansion team to the National League and hired George Weiss…

item.title: 1958: Mel Ott, 49, Critically Injured in Automobile Accident
item.description: Hall-of-Fame slugger Mel Ott, whose 511 career home runs remain the all-time National League record, is critically injured in an automobile accident in Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. The longtime New York Giants star, whose #4 uniform was retired in 1949, dies seven days later at the age of 49. (See Deaths below for November 21.) Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1953: Jimmy Dykes Named First Manager of Reborn Orioles
item.description: Jimmy Dykes becomes the first manager of the reborn Baltimore Orioles, ten days after his release from the same position with the Philadelphia Athletics. In October, Arthur Ehlers, former Philadelphia general manager, made the same switch to Baltimore. The Orioles are the transplanted St. Louis Browns, set to rejoin the American League after a 52-year absence in 1954. Photo: Bain News Service, publisher (Public domain).

item.title: 1946: Ted Williams Wins First AL MVP, Leads Red Sox to Flag
item.description: Ted Williams wins his first-ever BBWAA American League MVP Award. The 28-year-old "Splendid Splinter" helped his Boston Red Sox capture their first AL flag since 1918—the year of Williams' birth—leading his circuit in runs scored (142), bases on balls received (156), on-base percentage (.497), slugging percentage (.667), OPS (1.164), total bases (343) and bWAR (10.4); and coming in second to Mickey Vernon in batting… Photo: Apex Photo Company (Public domain).

item.title: 1942: Cubs Buy Contract of Ival Goodman, 34, From Reds
item.description: The Chicago Cubs purchase the contract of two-time former NL All-Star outfielder Ival Goodman, 34, from the Cincinnati Reds.

item.title: 1929: Joe McGinnity, 58, Hall of Fame Pitcher With 246 Wins
item.description: Joe McGinnity, 58, Hall of Fame pitcher whose 246 victories included eight 20-win seasons, while leading the National League in wins five times, in innings four times and games six times, as his 31 wins for the 1903 New York Giants included three complete August doubleheaders, and also won 239 games in the minor leagues. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).

item.title: 1889: Kansas City Cowboys Leave American Association for Western League
item.description: The Kansas City Cowboys drop out of the American Association in order to join the Western League.

item.title: 1889: Cincinnati Reds Leave American Association for National League
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds left the American Association on November 14, 1889, and joined the National League along with the Brooklyn Bridegrooms after a dispute with St. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1887: Cleveland Blues Unveil Web-Pattern Uniforms, Adopt Spiders Nickname
item.description: The Cleveland Blues announce new uniforms for the 1888 season. The web-like pattern on the uniform will inspire the nickname "Spiders" which the club officially adopts. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
